slides.headline: How much down payment do you really need?
bullets: UAE nationals: 20% down on a first home (30% above AED 5M)
Expat residents: 25% down on a first home (35% above AED 5M)
Off-plan property: 50% down, for everyone
slides.caption_fb:
Down payment rules in the UAE aren't one-size-fits-all — they're set by Central Bank Regulation No. 31/2013 and depend on your nationality status and the property itself.

Want the exact figure for your situation? Our mortgage calculator at {site_url} runs the full matrix — or WhatsApp us at {whatsapp_display}.

slides.headline: First home vs second property vs off-plan
bullets: Second property: 35% down for nationals, 40% for expats
Off-plan: always 50% down, regardless of nationality
Non-residents: typically 35–40% down — set by bank policy, not the Central Bank
slides.caption_fb:
Your down payment doesn't just depend on who you are — it depends on what you're buying. A second property and an off-plan unit both carry higher down payments than a first home, and non-resident figures come from bank policy rather than a fixed Central Bank rule.

We'll walk you through exactly what applies to your case. WhatsApp {whatsapp_display} or visit {site_url}.

slides.headline: The upfront costs beyond your down payment
bullets: DLD transfer fee: 4% of the property price + AED 580
Mortgage registration: 0.25% of the loan + AED 290
Plus a property valuation fee and the bank's arrangement fee
slides.caption_fb:
The down payment isn't the only cash you need on closing day. Dubai Land Department transfer fees, mortgage registration, valuation and arrangement fees all add up on top — and it's easy to be caught off guard by them.

Our calculator at {site_url} breaks all of it down for your exact numbers, or WhatsApp {whatsapp_display}.

slides.headline: How much can you actually borrow?
bullets: UAE banks cap your total monthly debt at 50% of gross income
Credit cards count as 5% of your card limit — not your balance
Whatever's left of that 50% is what can go toward a mortgage
slides.caption_fb:
This is the rule that surprises most first-time buyers: UAE banks count your credit card commitment as 5% of your card LIMIT, not what you actually owe on it. A high limit you never use in full still eats into your borrowing power.

Want to know your real number? Our affordability calculator at {site_url} does the math, or WhatsApp {whatsapp_display}.

slides.headline: The income-multiple cap most buyers miss
bullets: UAE nationals: banks cap borrowing at 8x annual income
Expat residents: the cap is 7x annual income
Your real limit is the smallest of this, the 50% rule, and the LTV cap
slides.caption_fb:
There isn't just one ceiling on your mortgage — there are three, and the smallest one wins. Alongside the 50% debt-burden rule and the down-payment (LTV) cap, banks also apply an income-multiple cap: 8x annual income for nationals, 7x for expats.

We check all three for you before you ever talk to a bank. WhatsApp {whatsapp_display} or visit {site_url}.

slides.headline: Resident vs non-resident: how it differs
bullets: Down payments run higher for non-residents — usually 35–40%
These figures are bank policy, not a Central Bank rule — they vary by lender
That's exactly where comparing lenders saves you the most
slides.caption_fb:
If you don't live in the UAE, your mortgage math looks a little different — higher down payments, and figures that vary by bank rather than a single fixed rule. That variation is exactly why comparing lenders matters more, not less, for non-residents.

We work with non-resident buyers regularly. WhatsApp {whatsapp_display} or visit {site_url}.

slides.headline: Is refinancing worth it?
bullets: Refinancing swaps your current mortgage for better rates or terms
Worth exploring when your rate, life circumstances, or the market has changed
We compare refinance offers the same way we compare a first mortgage
slides.caption_fb:
Your first mortgage doesn't have to be your last deal. If rates have moved, your income has changed, or you just haven't checked in a while, it's worth seeing what a refinance could do for your monthly payment.

We run the comparison the same way we do for a first-time buyer — free, no pressure. WhatsApp {whatsapp_display} or visit {site_url}.
